takeaways.t: **US-mediated talks between Ukrainian and Russian delegations ran for four hours in Abu Dhabi on 10 Nov, the first trilateral round since February;** President Zelensky said an exchange of 1,000 or 1,500 prisoners on each side was discussed, and Foreign Minister Lavrov said Russia “will not agree” to a truce. [6, 10, 11]

**UK counter-terror police arrested a 41-year-old senior US Army soldier near Gloucester on 10 Nov on suspicion of spying for Russia;** the BBC says he served at Imjin Barracks, home of NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, and police say the case is not linked to RAF Fairford. [12, 13]

**The Justice Department unsealed an eight-count indictment on 10 Nov charging three men with directing nearly 20 attacks and attempts in the US and Europe for the IRGC and Kataib Hezbollah,** including three vans sent to RAF Fairford on 26 Sep; Iran denies involvement. [14, 15]

**The House voted 211–204 on 10 Nov to refer Rep. Massie's impeachment articles against Secretary Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee,** so no vote on impeachment itself took place; the Senate confirmed Lt. Gen. Kevin Admiral the same evening to command US Army Europe and Africa and NATO's Allied Land Command. [16, 17]

**Poland's Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said after meeting Secretary Hegseth on 10 Nov that talks on a permanent US base in Poland were “going in the right direction”;** he said the White House decides in early December. [19, 20]

items.h: Abu Dhabi talks end first day after four hours, with a prisoner swap discussed
items.body: US-mediated talks between Ukrainian and Russian delegations opened in Abu Dhabi on 10 Nov, the first trilateral round since February, and ran four hours. [6, 22] Jared Kushner told the delegates at the opening: “We’ve had almost daily conversations with both sides and we’ve identified now where the gaps still fall short. We have some ideas to bridge them.” [23] President Zelensky said the sides discussed humanitarian steps, security guarantees and de-escalation, and later that an exchange of 1,000 or 1,500 prisoners on each side was raised and that the Russian side raised territory, which he called a matter for leaders. [24, 10] Secretary of State Rubio said in Paris on 10 Nov: “This is not something that can be resolved in the next 24 hours.” [22] Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on 10 Nov that a truce would let Kyiv regroup: “We will not agree to it.” [11]
items.next: The second day runs on 11 Nov on de-escalation, energy, the Black Sea, a prisoner exchange and a possible leaders' meeting, Zelensky said; the European Political Community meets in Dublin on 12 Nov. [10, 25]

items.h: Russia launches 162 drones and a missile overnight as drones hit Ust-Luga port
items.body: The Air Force said Russia launched one Iskander-M ballistic missile and 162 Shahed-type drones, 96 of them jet-powered, from 18:00 on 9 Nov; 135 drones were downed or suppressed by 07:30 on 10 Nov, with hits at 19 locations. [26] Between 06:30 and 19:00 on 10 Nov it counted 155 more Shahed-type drones, two Kh-59/69 missiles and Bandrol munitions, and 138 targets downed. [27] Leningrad Oblast governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said a drone hit the Ust-Luga port zone overnight into 11 Nov, starting a fire, and that 146 drones were downed over the region. [28, 29] The General Staff said a drone attack overnight into 10 Nov caused explosions and a fire at the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa, which services A-50 aircraft. [30]
items.next: Putin hosts the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) council in Moscow on 11 Nov, after talks with Lukashenko that ran almost four hours on 10 Nov. [31]

items.h: US charges three men over an Iranian-backed plot at RAF Fairford
items.body: The Justice Department charged three men on 10 Nov whom it described as acting for the IRGC and Iraq's Kataib Hezbollah over nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks in the US and Europe, including a plot at RAF Fairford; one is already in jail in New York. [15] Prosecutors say a group was paid to disguise vans as fuel delivery vehicles and drove them to the base, some carrying fuel barrels; Iran denies involvement. [15] Interfax, citing the New York Times, reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved from his Washington home to a military base over Iranian threats. [32] Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Israelis are “working overtime to drag the US into an endless war with Iran”; a fire on a South Pars gas platform was put out on 10 Nov and all 17 workers were rescued. [33, 34]
items.next: No date is set for US–Iran talks: security chief Mohsen Rezaei dismissed reports of talks with Washington. [33]

items.h: Romania and Bulgaria plan a Black Sea security centre in Constanța and Varna
items.body: Romanian President Nicușor Dan said on 10 Nov that Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye are setting up a Black Sea maritime security centre with a dual location in Constanța and Varna, toward which the Commission pledged €50 million in Bucharest on 9 Nov. [35] He said the three countries' joint mine-clearing operation was widened at NATO's Ankara summit to protect critical infrastructure. [35] At the naval academy in Varna on 10 Nov, with Prime Minister Rumen Radev, Commission President von der Leyen said: “the intention of these attacks is clear: Russia wants to spread fear and uncertainty in Europe.” [36] Russia's foreign ministry expelled a Moldovan embassy staff member on 10 Nov in reply to Moldova's expulsion of a Russian embassy employee on 23 Oct over a drone carrying explosives, calling Moldova's decision “another unfriendly step”. [37]
items.next: Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova is due to visit Romania in December, Dan said. [35]

items.h: Israel's new Knesset is sworn in as a UNIFIL patrol comes under fire
items.body: Israel's new Knesset was sworn in on 10 Nov; Gadi Eisenkot, whose four-party bloc holds 48 of 120 seats against 53 for Benjamin Netanyahu's, has 28 days to form a government, with a possible two-week extension. [38] UNIFIL said “about a dozen rounds” were fired at one of its patrols near Wadi Jilu in Tyre district on 10 Nov; the patrol returned fire and there were no casualties. [39] French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said G7 foreign ministers in Paris agreed on “the need to avoid a security void” in Lebanon after UNIFIL's mandate ends, and that there was no breakthrough on replacing the force. [39]
items.next: Eisenkot's 28 days run to about 6 Dec; UNIFIL's mandate ends on 31 Dec. [38, 39]

feature.title: PLA aircraft around Taiwan by the month: 3,125 sorties in a year
body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense publishes a report each morning counting the PLA aircraft sorties, navy ships and official ships it detected around Taiwan in the 24 hours to 06:00. Added up by report date, the twelve months from November 2025 to October 2026 come to 3,125 sorties, a mean of about 260 a month. December 2025 was the highest month at 492 and March 2026 the lowest at 162; October 2026 counted 223. [40]

One report sets the year's peak. For the 24 hours to 06:00 on 30 Dec 2025 the ministry counted 130 sorties, 90 of them across the median line into northern, central, southwestern and eastern airspace, with 14 navy ships and eight official ships; the next morning's report counted 77. [41, 40] Al Jazeera reported that China's two-day drills, Justice Mission 2025, ran on 29–30 Dec with live fire in five zones around Taiwan, according to the Eastern Theatre Command. [42] Outside those two reports, none in the twelve months exceeded 42 sorties, the count of 13 Feb 2026. [43, 40]
The months with the most reports recording no PLA aircraft were March 2026 with 12, February with 10 and June with 8; over the twelve months, 61 reports counted none. [40]

November opened higher. The report of 3 Nov counted 49 sorties, 31 of them entering central, southwestern and eastern airspace, the highest single count since 31 Dec 2025, and the first 11 reports of the month total 170. [44, 40] The report of 11 Nov counted four sorties, two across the median line, with seven navy ships and three official ships. [45]
after: Totals summed by the morning run from all 376 of the ministry's daily reports dated 1 Nov 2025 to 11 Nov 2026; each report covers 06:00 the previous day to 06:00 on its date, and the chart stops at October. [40]

leads.title: US indicts three over an Iran-backed plot at RAF Fairford, home to US bombers
leads.teaser: The indictment ties September's fuel-laden vans at the Gloucestershire base to the Revolutionary Guards and Kataib Hezbollah.
rows: The Justice Department unsealed an eight-count indictment on 10 Nov against Mohammad Ali al-Hassani, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi for nearly 20 attacks and attempts in the US and Europe for the IRGC and Kataib Hezbollah, including seven in the UK this spring. [14, 15]

Prosecutors say al-Hassani paid for perimeter surveillance on 22 Aug, then for vans, fuel barrels and possible shrapnel, and on 26 Sep sent three vans in delivery livery to the base; a roadblock turned at least two back. [14]
A4: charged in Manhattan, after two Britons were charged in the UK in October. Iran's embassy in London “categorically rejects” any link. [14, 15]

FBI Director Kash Patel: “This eight-count indictment shows the determination of Iran to commit terrorist attacks in Europe and the US.” At least a dozen US aircraft left RAF Mildenhall on 10 Nov after what the Wall Street Journal called a threat from Iran. [14, 15]
Prosecutors have not said where Mohajeri and al-Hassani are; al-Saadi has been held without bail in New York since May. [15]
leads.sw: Paid local helpers in commercial liveries reached a US base perimeter, which puts vehicle approaches and contractor vetting on the host-nation police agenda for every US-used site in the JOA.

leads.title: UK counter-terror police arrest a US Army soldier on suspicion of spying for Russia
leads.teaser: The 41-year-old senior soldier was based at Imjin Barracks, home of NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, the BBC understands.
rows: Counter Terrorism Policing London arrested him near Gloucester on 10 Nov under the National Security Act 2023 for obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service. [12, 13]
Imjin Barracks, Innsworth, per the BBC; police say it is not linked to Fairford. [12, 13]
A2: Russia named at arrest, no charge yet. [12]

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commanding general of US Army Counterintelligence Command: “The alleged conduct of a senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.” [12]
Police can hold him without charge for up to 14 days, to about 24 Nov. [12]
leads.sw: A suspected insider at a NATO corps headquarters is the case for re-briefing staff on the Threat Awareness and Reporting Program duty under AR 381-12 and reviewing who holds multinational planning products.

pattern: **Iran's European campaign reaches a US court:** the Fairford indictment links paid UK helpers to the IRGC, a day after France named the IRGC for the fridge sabotage. [14, 51]
**Insider threat at a NATO corps headquarters:** a senior US soldier, at the ARRC's barracks according to the BBC, is held on suspicion of spying for Russia. [12]
**Allies split on the November fridge wave:** Berlin warns Tehran without a finding, Brussels sees no Iranian link, and Iran denies. [54, 53, 51]
**Baltic alerts two nights running:** drones crossed Latvia on 9–10 Nov and an object from Belarus set off alerts in Lithuania on 10–11 Nov. [47, 48]

europe.h: De Wever's one-on-ones bring no breakthrough, and he skips Dublin for the budget
europe.body: Prime Minister Bart De Wever's bilateral budget talks since 9 Nov have produced no breakthrough, RTBF reported, citing negotiators who found his tables barely changed. [58] He is testing MR leader Georges-Louis Bouchez's idea of reopening the coalition agreement, which would add weeks, and has dropped the Dublin summits to work on the budget. [58] He reports to King Philippe on Mon 16 Nov. [58]
europe.sw: Provisional twelfths run at least until 16 Nov, holding SHAPE's host nation to this year's defence and host-nation-support spending.

europe.h: Dublin readies Ireland's largest security operation for 50 leaders at Thursday's EPC
europe.body: About 50 leaders meet in Dublin on Thu 12 Nov for the ninth European Political Community (EPC) summit, with Macron, Zelensky, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Merz expected; EU leaders meet informally on Fri 13 Nov. [59, 46] More than 5,000 gardaí (Irish police) are deployed, backed by other European police and militaries. [46] Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly said the senders of recent hoax threats want to “sow discord” and “destabilise democracies”. [46]
europe.sw: The EPC seats NATO's Secretary General with the UK and Ukraine, making Dublin the leaders' first joint setting after the Abu Dhabi talks.

europe.h: Taiwan says it has no plans to rename its Vilnius office as Chinese diplomats arrive
europe.body: Taiwan's Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi said on 10 Nov: “Currently, there are no plans to change the name,” after Delfi reported that Vilnius had asked for a new name. [60] Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius said on 9 Nov that Lithuania sets no preconditions for the talks. [61] Chinese diplomats are due this week; Lithuania has had no Chinese diplomatic staff since May 2025. [60]
europe.sw: Restored ties would return Chinese diplomats to a forward-land-forces host nation, a counter-intelligence factor for staff rotating through Lithuania.

countries.h: Merz offers Hungary German LNG and names air defence for joint work under SAFE
countries.body: Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Prime Minister Péter Magyar held the first German–Hungarian intergovernmental consultations in Berlin on 10 Nov; Merz offered to sell Hungary liquefied natural gas (LNG), and both named air defence, fundable from the EU's Security Action for Europe (SAFE) loan, as the lead defence topic [18]. Magyar said “Árkérdések vannak, még meg kell egyeznünk” (“There are price questions, we still have to agree”) and rejected tying the EU budget to Ukraine aid [18, 62]. Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi told Boris Pistorius that Hungary is ready to take a larger role in Europe's conventional defence and named drones, missiles, ammunition and military AI for industrial work [63]. Magyar invited Merz to Budapest in the spring [18].
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 2 (resilient energy supplies): German LNG would add a western gas source beside Russian gas via TurkStream, with price still open.

q.t: A kontinens jövőjével kapcsolatban biztosítottam partneremet arról, hogy Magyarország kész nagyobb szerepet vállalni Európa hagyományos védelmében, és támogatja az ezt szolgáló közös erőfeszítéseket is.
q.en: On the future of the continent, I assured my counterpart that Hungary is ready to take a larger role in Europe's conventional defence and supports the joint efforts that serve it.

countries.h: Hungarian police disclose first case of a fake mobile base station run from a car
countries.body: Police, the communications authority NMHH and the operator Yettel disclosed on 10 Nov Hungary's first case of a fake mobile base station: run from a moving car, it disrupted an operator's network and sent phishing texts posing as the police [64]. Investigators logged 88,235 network events on 13–22 July and tracked the car from Budapest to Pécs, where a 27-year-old Chinese man was arrested on 22 July; he is in custody [64, 65].
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 6 (resilient civil communications): one transmitter in a car degraded a commercial network as it moved, and the operator's anomaly monitoring caught it.

q.t: Közérdekű üzem ellen elkövetett információs rendszer vagy adat megsértésével gyanúsítja az NNI azt a férfit, aki mozgó gépkocsiból működtetett, hamis mobil-bázisállomással zavart meg egy szolgáltatói hálózatot, és rendőrségi értesítésnek álcázott adathalász SMS-eket küldött.
q.en: The NNI suspects the man of breaching an information system or data of a public-interest utility; he disrupted an operator's network with a fake mobile base station run from a moving car and sent phishing texts disguised as police notices.

countries.h: Slovak coalition falls one vote short of moving its cooperating-witness bill
countries.body: Only 75 of the 150 deputies present voted on 10 Nov to move the coalition's amendment on cooperating defendants, the kajúcnici (penitents), into third reading, so it stalled [66]. Non-attached deputies Tomáš Taraba, Roman Malatinec and Peter Slyško voted with the opposition, which says the change would help Deputy Speaker Tibor Gašpar; he denies it [66, 67]. The vote is repeated on 11 Nov at 11:00 [66].
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 1 (continuity of government): with 75 secure votes of 150, every bill, deployment mandates included, now turns on three non-attached deputies.

q.t: Za návrh na postúpenie do tretieho čítania hlasovalo zo 150 prítomných poslancov len 75.
q.en: Of the 150 deputies present, only 75 voted for the motion to move it to third reading.

countries.h: Slovakia and Czechia agree joint buying of rescue gear and study reverse Druzhba flow
countries.body: At a joint Slovak–Czech cabinet session in Bratislava on 10 Nov, the fire and rescue services signed a joint procurement contract covering hardened tanker engines and personnel carriers, firefighting robots, flood and hazardous-material kit and evacuation buses [68]. Economy Minister Denisa Saková said the two countries have tested emergency diesel deliveries and are examining reverse oil flow through Druzhba, about €41 million on the Czech side [69].
countries.sw: Baseline requirements 5 and 2 (mass casualties, energy): pooled rescue fleets and a studied Druzhba reverse flow from Czechia widen Slovakia's options beyond the line through Ukraine.

q.t: Slovensko-česká spolupráca podľa nej už priniesla dohody o uskladňovaní plynu či testy núdzových dodávok nafty, pričom krajiny preverujú aj reverznú prepravu ropy cez Družbu s odhadovanou investíciou 41 miliónov eur na českej strane.
q.en: According to her, Slovak–Czech cooperation has already brought agreements on gas storage and tests of emergency diesel deliveries, and the countries are also examining reverse transport of oil through Druzhba, with an estimated investment of €41 million on the Czech side.

countries.h: German conscientious-objection claims reach 16,869, over four times last year's total
countries.body: The Federal Office for Family and Civil Society Tasks (BAFzA) received 16,869 applications for conscientious objection from 1 Jan to 31 Oct, against 3,879 in all of 2025; almost 1,900 came in October [70]. The rise follows the Wehrdienst-Modernisierungsgesetz (military service modernisation law), which since January requires young men to fill in a questionnaire and undergo screening [70, 71]. Defence Minister Boris Pistorius expects to cover personnel needs without conscription [71].
countries.sw: Wehrdienst law: its compulsory fallback turns on whether volunteers meet the targets, and objections now arrive at about 1,900 a month from the same cohort.

q.t: Vom 1. Januar bis 31. Oktober sind insgesamt 16.869 Anträge auf Kriegsdienstverweigerung eingegangen, wie eine Sprecherin des BAFzA mitteilte.
q.en: From 1 January to 31 October a total of 16,869 applications for conscientious objection were received, a BAFzA spokeswoman said.

countries.h: Lukashenko thanks Putin for the newest weapons and Russian forces kept in the west
countries.body: Meeting Vladimir Putin at Novo-Ogaryovo on 10 Nov, the eve of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) summit in Moscow, Aleksandr Lukashenko said Belarus has mastered everything Russia promised on security, in the state's own words as published by BelTA: “Все виды вооружений, самые новые” (“All types of weapons, the newest”) [72]. He thanked Putin for keeping combat-ready “те формирования, которые вы создали, и на западе держите на всякий случай” (“those formations that you created and keep in the west just in case”) and said they were never sent to the combat zone in Ukraine [72].
countries.sw: Eastern-flank posture: Minsk says the Russian formations on its western direction, facing Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, are kept combat-ready and out of the war.

countries.h: Wang Yi asks Slovakia to keep playing a constructive role in EU–China relations
countries.body: Foreign Minister Wang Yi met Slovakia's Juraj Blanár in Beijing on 10 Nov; the ministry's readout says, in the state's own words: “希望斯方继续为中欧关系稳健发展发挥建设性作用” (“We hope Slovakia will continue to play a constructive role in the steady development of China–EU relations”) [73]. The same day the Slovak firm Nuclear Power signed memoranda with China General Nuclear (CGN) and China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC) [74].
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 2 (resilient energy supplies): China's two state nuclear groups now hold memoranda with a Slovak nuclear firm, a supplier question in a priority country's critical infrastructure.

euregio.h: Vynova files for bankruptcy in Tessenderlo as its Chemelot restart seeks a payment freeze
euregio.body: Chemicals maker Vynova filed for bankruptcy at its Tessenderlo-Ham site on 10 Nov, costing 600 jobs; UHasselt economist Piet Pauwels blames overcapacity in chlorine compounds for PVC and Europe's energy prices. [75] The same day LVM Netherlands, the restart of the bankrupt Vynova Beek plant on Chemelot, applied for suspension of payments, De Limburger reported. [76]
euregio.sw: Two Vynova plants in trouble either side of the border belong in J9's economic-resilience picture of the Limburgs.

euregio.h: Benelux prime ministers and NRW's Wüst meet in Maastricht on cross-border services
euregio.body: Prime Minister Rob Jetten hosted Belgium's Bart De Wever and Luxembourg's Luc Frieden in Maastricht on 10 Nov for the Benelux summit, joined later by North Rhine-Westphalia's Hendrik Wüst. [77, 78] The programme covered cross-border police and ambulance projects and autonomous road transport; De Limburger noted that Jetten and De Wever are both under fire at home. [78, 79]
euregio.sw: Cross-border police and ambulance arrangements are the civil layer host-nation support around Brunssum rests on.

items.h: Northern navies sign a pact aboard HMS Prince of Wales as Rutte heads to Oslo
items.body: Navy chiefs of the UK-led Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) signed a Northern Navies Initiative aboard HMS Prince of Wales in Oslo on 10 Nov, to train to one standard, plan before a crisis and build interoperable equipment. [7] The UK says the aim is a JEF that acts as NATO's maritime vanguard in the North Atlantic, High North and Baltic and can “transition seamlessly into NATO command”. [7] Secretary General Rutte speaks on the same carrier today at 18:10 and with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting at 18:50. [80]
items.sw: A JEF built to hand over to NATO command feeds the north-eastern maritime picture behind JFC Brunssum's land plans.

items.h: Bundeswehr retires Chinese commercial drones and plans to bar Chinese cars from barracks
items.body: The Bundeswehr has ordered units to stop using commercial drones from the large Chinese makers and to replace them with national or European products, Spiegel reported on 10 Nov [81, 82]. The defence ministry fears the drones pass data on exercises, barracks and weapon systems to Chinese intelligence, and the Bundeswehr also intends to bar Chinese-made cars from barracks over their sensors [82].
items.sw: Host-nation support under Operationsplan Deutschland: the barracks and training areas that stage allied reinforcements are being closed to Chinese drones, and next to Chinese cars.

items.h: Poland trades two MiG-29s for Ukrainian counter-drone know-how
items.body: Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk said on 10 Nov he had signed an agreement in Kyiv setting up Polish-Ukrainian working groups on drone and counter-drone technology. [83] Poland will hand over two more MiG-29s past their service life in exchange for that technology, in a package of about €50 million; it has given Ukraine 14 since March 2023. [84, 83]
items.sw: Counter-drone methods adopted by Poland feed the eastern-flank threat picture JFC Brunssum plans against.

items.h: US Air Force CCAs fly in formation under Shield AI's autonomy for the first time
items.body: Shield AI said its Hivemind software flew several Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) in formation through beyond-visual-range counter-air tactics on 26 Oct, Defense News reported on 10 Nov. [85] The Air Force wants 500 combat-ready CCAs by 2032 and asked for $2.37 billion in FY27. [85] In Oslo, the First Sea Lord said he would sign with Northrop Grumman to prepare its Talon for Royal Navy trials, with a carrier demonstration planned for 2027. [86]
items.sw: Uncrewed combat aircraft add a class of friendly air track to the airspace plans NATO land headquarters write.

items.h: Allen Control Systems opens a laser division for counter-drone weapons
items.body: Allen Control Systems, maker of the Bullfrog autonomous gun station, launched a directed energy division on 10 Nov, led by two former directed-energy chiefs at the Army's Space and Missile Defense Command. [87] The company says Bullfrog rounds cost as little as $10, and former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll said this year the Pentagon had bought 12 Bullfrogs for the Iran war. [87] It named no laser product; the Army recently awarded AeroVironment up to $464.8 million for high-energy lasers. [87]
items.sw: A $10 round is the benchmark host nations weigh when they budget point defence for NATO and US sites.

items.h: Britain buys a £90 million drone and sensor net to watch North Atlantic cables
items.body: The UK announced on 10 Nov a £90 million framework with Ocean Infinity Solutions for Atlantic Net, the first phase of the Royal Navy's Atlantic Bastion programme. [88] Uncrewed systems, sensors and AI are to form one surveillance service, directed by the Navy, that warns submarine hunters of Russian submarines and threats to cables and energy networks. [88]
items.sw: Cables landing in the Netherlands and Belgium are host-nation critical infrastructure, and this service is one more feed for J9's hybrid-threat picture.

items.h: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to all paying developers and Ultra subscribers
items.body: Google DeepMind made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available on 10 Nov through the Gemini API for paying developers and to Google AI Ultra subscribers. [89] Artificial Analysis scored it 59 on its Intelligence Index v5, first overall, at $7.76 per index task against $10.04 for Claude Opus 5.5. [90] Introductory pricing is $2 per million input and $10 per million output tokens, which The Verge reports doubles at the end of November; Google is also previewing /swarm, which turns one prompt into a coordinated team of agents. [89, 91]
items.sw: Google’s demonstrations have /swarm teams turning planning PDFs and engineering drawings into 3D models, the material J9 handles, so check what Gemini for business retains before host-nation documents go in.

items.h: Claude Fable 5.2 leads DeepMind’s new test of agent work on drawings and scans
items.body: Google DeepMind and Artificial Analysis launched the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark on 10 Nov: 200 private tasks in 10 industries in which an agent reads drawings, schematics or scans and delivers decks, spreadsheets or reports, each graded on about 70 rubric criteria. [92] Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 leads with 57% of the harder criteria met, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon at 54% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 53%, but costs $31.97 per task against $6.29 for Carbon. [92] No model passes 52% on Word or text-file deliverables. [92]
items.sw: J9 work runs on these inputs, site plans, schematics and host-nation reports, and a five-fold cost gap for three points argues for the cheaper model on bulk review, with a human check on every deliverable.

items.h: Google adds a confidential-computing TPU and a dual-chip TPU 8i Max
items.body: Google announced two more eighth-generation TPU systems on 9 Nov, four in one year: TPU 8tx, designed with AMD, keeps data and model weights protected in hardware while in use, with up to 2x lower latency than TPU 8t, and TPU 8i Max packages two TPU 8i chips for double the compute, SRAM and HBM bandwidth. [93, 94] Google says TPUs have nearly 100 customers and pitches 8tx at regulated enterprises and governments running models on sensitive data. [93]
items.sw: Confidential inference is the technical precondition for running frontier models on classified or host-nation-sensitive data in a commercial cloud; ask whether NATO’s cloud plans list it as a requirement.

depth.title: M-SHORAD: 36 Strykers a battalion now, a pallet for any truck by late 2029
body: The Maneuver Short-Range Air Defense programme (M-SHORAD) is the Army's layer against drones and low-flying aircraft over its brigades. Increment 1, the Sgt Stout, is a Stryker with eight Stingers, an XM914 30 mm cannon, an M240 machine gun and a radar. The first plan was 144 systems in four battalions of 40; a battalion now has 36. Fielded: 5-4 Air Defense Artillery in Germany, 4-60 at Fort Sill, 6-56 at Fort Hood and two-thirds of 3-4 at Fort Bragg, complete by the end of FY2026; Guard battalions in Florida and Ohio follow in FY2028 and FY2029. [96]

The FY2027 request buys 14 Sgt Stouts for $712.7 million, about $51 million each in that line, a figure computed from the totals that covers more than the vehicle. Research and development adds $460.9 million: $215.1 million for the Stinger replacement, $94.8 million for directed-energy upgrades and $108.1 million for Increment 4. Increment 2, the 50 kW laser, will not be fielded. [96]

Increment 4 is the new piece. Slides from an October industry day in Huntsville, reported on 10 Nov, put the first battalion's equipment in October–December 2029 and initial capability in FY2030; CRS in April said late FY2029. It must be a pallet for a JLTV, an Infantry Squad Vehicle or a robotic vehicle, with no trailer, fight 72 hours alone and three to seven days with its supported force, and fit a C-130. [97, 96]

Targets run from quadcopters to Shahed 136-class drones in swarms, plus helicopters and attack aircraft. The Army leaves sensors and effectors open; L3Harris, Leidos, Leonardo DRS, Moog, SAIC and Sierra Nevada have shown designs. [97]

dod.h: Poland says Hegseth backs a permanent US base, with a White House call in December
dod.body: Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said after meeting Secretary Hegseth at the Pentagon on 10 Nov that Hegseth told him talks on a permanent US base in Poland were “going in the right direction”, which he read as a green light; the White House decides in early December. [19, 20] He said the posture review is nearing completion, a Polish Tomahawk request has a positive Pentagon answer pending Congress, and the two signed a defence-industrial agreement. [20, 19, 101] Ambassador Whitaker told Defence24 that announcements on Poland will follow the review. [102]
dod.sw: A permanent base in Poland fixes where US Army units sit on the eastern flank, the baseline for the reinforcement plans JFC Brunssum coordinates.

dod.h: Twelve US tankers leave Mildenhall as two English bases go to FPCON Charlie
dod.body: Ten KC-135s left RAF Mildenhall on 9 Nov and two more on 10 Nov for Spangdahlem, Ramstein, Morón and Prestwick, and three CV-22s moved to Lakenheath, The War Zone reported; The Wall Street Journal tied the moves to an Iranian threat, with both bases at Force Protection Condition Charlie. [95, 103] US Air Forces in Europe declined to comment on intelligence; Prime Minister Burnham's spokesman said Britain's bases were safe. [95, 103] A US indictment returned on 10 Nov alleges one of three charged men orchestrated the September plot at RAF Fairford for an Iran-aligned network. [95]
dod.sw: Tankers moved to Spangdahlem and Ramstein add to the host-nation support load on German airfields.

news.h: Police arrest a senior US soldier in England on suspicion of spying for Russia
news.body: British police arrested a 41-year-old US soldier near Gloucester on 10 Nov under sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act, on suspicion of obtaining protected information and assisting Russian intelligence. [104] Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commander of Army Counterintelligence Command: “The alleged conduct of a senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.” [104] Police said the case is not linked to other counter-terrorism investigations; the soldier and unit were not named. [104]

congress.h: House sends Hegseth impeachment articles to Judiciary on a 211–204 vote
congress.body: The House voted 211–204 on 10 Nov to refer Rep. Massie's eight articles against Secretary Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, a step Massie called a “procedural motion to kill the resolution”; tagesschau says Republicans voted almost as a bloc. [16, 105] The committee need not act, and Democrats take the House in January. [16, 99] Hegseth had called Massie a “disgruntled and defeated congressman” that morning. [99]
congress.sw: Hegseth stays through the lame duck, so the posture and Poland base decisions remain his to sign.

congress.body: The Senate confirmed Lt. Gen. Kevin D. Admiral on 10 Nov in its evening wrap-up, with 19 other military calendar items reported on 23 Sep. [17, 106] They include Maj. Gen. Christopher R. Norrie, acting USAREUR-AF commander since 2 Jul, and Lt. Gens. Edmond M. Brown and Francisco J. Lozano, each to be lieutenant general in a post the log does not name. congress.h: Senate agrees to vote by 20 Nov on a House resolution to end Iran hostilities
congress.body: Senators agreed on 10 Nov to discharge H.Con.Res. 93 from Foreign Relations and vote on it by Fri 20 Nov after six hours of debate. [17] Rep. Seth Moulton's resolution directs the President under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove US forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress authorises them. [108] The White House said on 15 Sep that such resolutions “lack the force of law”. [109]
congress.sw: US bases in Britain and Germany carried the Iran campaign's bombers and tankers, so the vote bears on what host nations are asked to support.

research.title: Managing Russia’s Military-Industrial Degradation: Navigating Wartime Industrial Constraints, Stockpile Exhaustion, and Hardware Attrition
research.authors: Mathieu Boulègue, Federico Borsari, Pavel Luzin
summary: The authors assess whether Russia’s military-industrial complex (OPK) can meet the demands of the war and conclude that the Kremlin “has only postponed addressing the OPK’s many problems.” [21] Output is squeezed between exhaustion, the running down and constant repair of Soviet-era stocks, and attrition, the limited ability to build new systems faster than they are consumed; inputs are squeezed by shortages of machine tools, special steels, explosives chemicals and microelectronics. [21] Surge production keeps equipment flowing “by simplifying production, lowering quality, and ultimately sacrificing long-term capacity for short-term battlefield endurance.” [21]

Drones and missiles are the exception: the report describes a “dronization” of the industry and cites a Ukrainian analyst putting missile output at 120–150% of expenditure. [21] The authors expect no collapse but an uneven tipping point, earlier in heavy armour, later in missiles and drones, and a “managed degradation” that sustains the war in the short to medium term; a “low-tech” Russia “will not necessarily mean a Kremlin that is less dangerous, aggressive, or prone to risk and escalation.” [21] They recommend sanctions on industrial inputs and continued military aid to Ukraine. [21]
findings: **Armour:** nearly 15,000 vehicles pulled from storage since 2022, 7,500–8,200 left, about 4,790 refurbishable; 2025 output of new and refurbished armoured fighting vehicles about 3,700, a third new, against more than 13,500 visually confirmed destroyed. [21]

**Shells:** domestic production rose about 10% in 2025 to 1.717 million, while a leak shows some 5.3 million supplied; the authors put most of the gap down to 8–11 million North Korean shells in 2023–2025. [21]
**Missiles:** Kh-101 output rose from 56 in 2021 to an estimated 633 in 2025; Iskander-M from about 40 a month in early 2024 to as many as 70 by mid-2025. [21]

**Drones:** a General Staff requirement, reported by analyst Rob Lee, of at least 87,000 one-way attack drones in 2026; the State Defence Order plans 48,000 Geran-2 and Gerbera strike systems, at about $70,000 a unit. [21]
research.method: A qualitative assessment built from Russian official and corporate data, leaked contract documents examined by Ukrainian private intelligence firms, OSINT estimates and an expert workshop on 21 Apr 2026. Many vehicle figures are third-party estimates the authors call fragmentary; several missile and drone numbers come from Ukrainian analysts and leaks; US European Command’s Russia Strategic Initiative funded the work. [21]
research.sw: For Brunssum: with armour reserves running down and missile and drone lines growing, civil preparedness reviews against baseline requirements 2 and 7 (energy, transport) in the JOA should be measured against long-range strike and drones, not Russia’s tank count.

research.org: Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology, Fudan University and partners (Nature Communications)
research.title: Archival and palaeoenvironmental documentation of extreme climate events reveals generational amnesia in collective memory
research.authors: Shuang Song, Bo Hu, David Max Findley, Xutong Wu, Wei Liu, Robert W. Middeke-Conlin, Victor L. Caetano-Andrade, Yuda Yang, Shuai Wang, Jürgen Renn, Patrick Roberts
research.length: research article, open access, with supplementary data
summary: The authors set Chinese written records of floods and droughts in the Yellow River Basin from 1470 to 1900, drawn from official histories, local gazetteers, diaries and inscriptions, against tree-ring reconstructions of summer rain and river flow. [110] The mismatches are not random: record-keepers judged a year’s severity against recent experience rather than the long-run climate. [110] Re-standardising the tree-ring series against a sliding baseline of 20–40 years, roughly one generation, raises its correlation with the archives, and an agent-based model reproduces the pattern when people judge climate against their own lived memory (“generational amnesia”) but not against a shared archive. [110] The authors read archives as “behaviourally transformed climate signals” and call for bias-aware corrections in risk assessment. [110]
findings: **Agreement:** over 208 years the two five-level series agree only modestly (Cohen’s weighted κ = 0.2, accuracy 0.39). [110]
**Generational window:** the best window averages 33 years across two-century segments and raises the correlation by up to 19.65%. [110]
**Model:** agents’ life expectancy is the dominant parameter and enough on its own to reproduce the offset. [110]
research.method: A historical wet/dry index from 32 archive sites compared with a tree-ring index, both in five levels, using confusion matrices, sliding-window re-standardisation and an agent-based model with sensitivity analysis. Both series are reconstructions, the tree-ring index correlates with instruments at only r = 0.35, archives carry institutional choices, and the case is one monsoon basin. [110]
research.sw: Flood and drought plans in Europe that lean on what residents and officials remember inherit the same generation-long baseline this study measures in four centuries of records.

research.org: NYU Grossman School of Medicine and NYU Center for Data Science (Nature Communications)
research.title: LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts future PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives with expert-level accuracy
research.authors: Victoria Mueller, Jyoti Yadav, Annie Farnsworth, Charlotte E. Hilberdink, Sapir Gershov, Eric K. Oermann, Stephen P. Wall, Arieh Y. Shalev, Katharina Schultebraucks
summary: About 27% of trauma patients in US emergency departments develop post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) within a month, yet only about 28% of departments screen for it, largely because questionnaires take 15 to 20 minutes. [111] The authors test whether the answer to one routine question, “Tell me about the event that brought you to the ED”, recorded within 24 hours, is enough. [111] PREVIA chains open-weight models: Llama and Mistral read the narrative along four clinical dimensions, DeepSeek summarises and a final model gives a 0–100 risk score with an explanation. [111] On 145 patients from two New York trauma centres, checked against the gold-standard CAPS-5 interview a month later, it beat single models including OpenAI’s o3 and matched an expert clinician; the authors call the results initial. [111]
findings: **Accuracy:** AUROC 78.49% and sensitivity 95.4%, with precision of 46.76%, across 145 patients. [111]
**Against a clinician:** on 30 random patients PREVIA reached AUROC 84.39% and sensitivity 100%, the clinician 83.86% and 88.89%. [111]
**Acceptability:** 38 of 572 eligible patients (6.6%) declined because of the video recording. [111]
research.method: A sub-study of an NIH-funded cohort: bedside video narratives transcribed with Whisper, a three-layer zero-shot ensemble, three-fold cross-validation and ablations, with diagnosis by CAPS-5 at one month. The sample is small, English-speaking and from one city; unstable and brain-injured patients were excluded; the clinician benchmark is one expert; and with precision below 50%, about half of those flagged did not develop PTSD. [111]
research.sw: European emergency departments and military medical services face the same time limits on PTSD screening, and this tests a one-question screener on open-weight models, which a hospital can host itself, against the clinical gold standard.

philosophy.work: Novum Organon Renovatum (The Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences, part two)
philosophy.where: Book II, chapter V (“Of Certain Characteristics of Scientific Induction”), section III (“Tests of Hypotheses”), article 11, pp. 87–88
philosophy.year: 1858 (third edition; the passage also stands in the 1847 second edition of The Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences, vol. 2, p. 65)
philosophy.tradition: Philosophy of science (Bacon, Whewell, Mill, Mach, Poincaré, Duhem, Fleck, Carnap, Popper, Kuhn, Lakatos, Feyerabend, Hacking, Cartwright, Longino)
philosophy.quote: “But the evidence in favour of our induction is of a much higher and more forcible character when it enables us to explain and determine cases of a kind different from those which were contemplated in the formation of our hypothesis. … No false supposition could, after being adjusted to one class of phenomena, exactly represent a different class, where the agreement was unforeseen and uncontemplated. That rules springing from remote and unconnected quarters should thus leap to the same point, can only arise from that being the point where truth resides.”
philosophy.translation: Whewell wrote in English: Novum Organon Renovatum, third edition (London: John W. Parker and Son, 1858), pp. 87–88, checked against the 1847 second edition of The Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences, vol. 2, p. 65; the ellipsis omits two sentences. [112, 113]
philosophy.gloss: Whewell ranks grades of confirmation: explaining what has been observed shows we know nature’s “alphabet”, predicting new cases of the same kind that we command her “language”, but a hypothesis fitted to one class of facts that turns out to fix a quite different class gives evidence of a higher order, since a false supposition tuned to the first class has no reason to match the second. [112] In the next paragraph he names this the “Consilience of Inductions”, with Newton’s inverse-square attraction, which explained Kepler’s third law and then his first and second, and universal gravitation, which also accounted for the precession of the equinoxes, as model cases; it sits among the tests of hypotheses beside prediction and coherence. [112, 114] The strongest objection is John Stuart Mill’s in A System of Logic (Book III, chapter XIV, §6): a hypothesis that already matches a phenomenon’s laws in many respects should match them “in one respect more”, and “Though twenty such coincidences should occur, they would not prove the reality of the undulatory ether.” [115] On Mill’s account consilience shows that two sets of laws are partly identical, not that the entity the theory posits exists. [115]
philosophy.why: When an assessment built from one stream of reports turns out to explain reports nobody fed into it, is that consilience, or only a model loose enough to fit anything?

deep.title: Arctic Sentry, seen from Moscow
body: NATO launched Arctic Sentry on 11 Feb, Mark Rutte said, in the face of “Russia’s increased military activity and China’s growing interest in the High North”, bringing allied activity “into one, overarching operational approach to the region”. [116] Today he is in Oslo for the Atlantic Future Forum aboard HMS Prince of Wales. [80] The allied assumption is that visible vigilance deters without raising the stakes. Seen from Moscow, the activity lands on a doctrine that already lists it as a threat.

Russia’s Maritime Doctrine of July 2022 classes the Russian Arctic and the waters of the Northern Sea Route as vital areas where, in the Indian defence institute MP-IDSA’s reading, Russia will use military force if necessary. [117] Its threats include NATO infrastructure near Russia’s borders, more exercises in nearby waters, efforts to weaken Russian control of the Northern Sea Route and a build-up of foreign naval presence in the Arctic, which now leads the regional chapters with 56 mentions against 33 in 2015. [117] Mathieu Boulègue noted that it calls for more control over foreign military activity in the sea and air approaches. [118] Arctic Sentry matches that list item by item.

Moscow said so before the first exercise. On 15 Jan the foreign ministry spokeswoman, Maria Zakharova, called the talk of the mission «очередную провокацию западных стран, которые пытаются насадить свои порядки» (“another provocation by Western countries that are trying to impose their own order”). [119] On 31 Aug Sergei Lavrov wrote, in Reuters’ translation, that “Such military activity in the Far North poses direct threats to Russia’s security.” [120] A SHAPE spokesman answered that NATO poses “no threat to anyone”. [121] In April 2024 Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko promised a proportionate answer to Finnish and Swedish accession, with the restored Moscow and Leningrad military districts and a new Karelian Corps cited as the measures. [122]

What Moscow guards there is its sea-based deterrent. Three of Russia’s eight Borei-class missile submarines serve with the Northern Fleet, and on 28 Oct a Bulava fired from the Sea of Okhotsk hit the Chizha range on the Kanin Peninsula during the US Global Thunder exercise. [123] From the Kremlin, persistent allied surveillance of the northern approaches is surveillance of its second-strike force, which is why the doctrine files these waters as vital, not merely important.

Moscow also reads the seams. On 11 Nov RIA Novosti, citing NRK, reported that Norway’s Jonas Gahr Støre does not rule out another call with Vladimir Putin after the one he and Finland’s Alexander Stubb held in late October, answering criticism from Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen. [124] The new US ambassador to Norway flew to Kirkenes on his first day, and Norway is placing NASAMS sensors on the border against stray drones. [125, 126] To a Russian planner that is vigilance that is real but national, with capitals keeping their own lines to Moscow.

The cheapest Russian answers are the ones already in use: statements, missile tests and, as the Troms and Finnmark county governor notes, GPS jamming in the north. [126] CEPA’s report of 10 Nov finds heavy-armour reserves running down while missile output, by a Ukrainian analyst’s estimate, runs at 120–150% of expenditure, which favours that menu. [21] Read from Moscow, the test of the allied plan is not whether Arctic Sentry deters an assault on Finnmark but whether it raises the price of this low-cost pressure.

items.h: Dutch-German rail pact leaves out an Eindhoven–Heerlen–Aachen intercity
items.body: State Secretary Annet Bertram and German transport minister Steffen Bilger signed a declaration in Berlin on 10 Nov for more and faster cross-border trains and room for new operators; no money is attached. [148, 149] It says nothing about the Eindhoven–Heerlen–Aachen intercity Limburg has long sought, which L1 now describes as at a dead end. [149] It does aim for heavier 740-metre trains, which NOS notes matters for moving tanks from Dutch ports to NATO's eastern territory; direct Amsterdam–Berlin trains stop for three months next spring for works. items.h: Heerlen puts the cost of a 2033 culture-capital title at about €70 million
items.body: Heerlen's culture alderman Theo de Groot told the council on 10 Nov that a European Capital of Culture 2033 title for Heerlen and Parkstad would cost about €70 million, mostly from the state, the EU, the province and sponsors. [150] At a 10% municipal share, Heerlen and Parkstad would pay about €7 million; the bid alone costs €800,000. [150] A motion by PVV, Hart-Leers and FVD to withdraw the bid failed. [150]
items.fy: Nothing to do; the bid runs for years.

items.h: Members' data copied from AllUnited, the club system used by 35 sports federations
items.body: Dutch sports clubs reported on 10 Nov that an attacker used a software flaw in AllUnited, a membership system for clubs and federations, to copy its database on 9 Nov; the flaw is now closed. [151] NU.nl reported all 35 federations on the system were hit; the data can include names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, IBAN numbers and log-ins. [151] The cricket federation KNCB warned of fake payment requests for fees or fines. [152]

items.nl: Oekraïne en Rusland praten weer met elkaar. Dat gebeurt in Abu Dhabi, met hulp van de Verenigde Staten. Het eerste gesprek duurde vier uur. Ze spraken onder meer over het ruilen van gevangenen. Vandaag praten ze verder.
items.en: Ukraine and Russia are talking to each other again. It is happening in Abu Dhabi, with help from the United States. The first meeting lasted four hours. They talked about exchanging prisoners, among other things. They continue today.

items.nl: Rusland viel Oekraïne opnieuw aan met drones. Het ging om 162 drones en één raket. Oekraïne schoot 135 drones neer. Oekraïense drones raakten ook een haven bij Sint-Petersburg. Daar ontstond een brand.
items.en: Russia attacked Ukraine with drones again. It involved 162 drones and one missile. Ukraine shot down 135 drones. Ukrainian drones also hit a port near St Petersburg. A fire broke out there.

items.nl: In Engeland heeft de politie een Amerikaanse militair opgepakt. De politie denkt dat hij voor Rusland spioneerde. De man is 41 jaar oud. Volgens de BBC werkte hij bij een hoofdkwartier van de NAVO.
items.en: In England the police have arrested an American soldier. The police think he spied for Russia. The man is 41 years old. According to the BBC he worked at a NATO headquarters.

items.kop: Merz wil gas verkopen aan Hongarije
items.nl: De Hongaarse premier Péter Magyar was dinsdag in Berlijn. Hij sprak daar met bondskanselier Friedrich Merz. Duitsland wil vloeibaar gas aan Hongarije verkopen. Over de prijs zijn ze het nog niet eens. De landen willen ook samenwerken aan luchtverdediging.
items.en: Hungary's Prime Minister Péter Magyar was in Berlin on Tuesday. He spoke there with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Germany wants to sell liquefied gas to Hungary. They do not yet agree on the price. The countries also want to work together on air defence.

items.nl: De Tweede Kamer heeft lang gepraat over het belastingplan voor 2027. Er is nog geen akkoord. Vandaag onderhandelen de partijen verder. Donderdag stemt de Kamer over het plan.
items.en: The Tweede Kamer has talked for a long time about the 2027 tax plan. There is no agreement yet. Today the parties negotiate further. On Thursday the Kamer votes on the plan.

items.nl: Heerlen en Parkstad willen in 2033 Culturele Hoofdstad van Europa worden. Dat kost ongeveer 70 miljoen euro. Het meeste geld komt van het Rijk, Europa, de provincie en sponsors. Een voorstel om te stoppen kreeg geen meerderheid.
items.en: Heerlen and Parkstad want to become European Capital of Culture in 2033. That costs about 70 million euros. Most of the money comes from the national government, Europe, the province and sponsors. A proposal to stop did not get a majority.

news.h: Välimäki and Nikishin compete for one blue-line spot in Helsinki
news.body: NHL.com reported on Tue 10 Nov that it is unclear whether Juuso Välimäki or Alexander Nikishin, who had a goal and an assist in his season debut on 7 Nov, will play against Seattle on Thursday [165]. Välimäki has two goals, one assist and a plus-7 in eight games since his recall, and returned to the NHL on 20 Oct after 632 days away [165, 166]. “First of all, he's played very, very well,” head coach Rod Brind’Amour told NHL.com; “we're real lucky to have him” [165]. Välimäki, from Tampere, called the trip “a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, really” after a 50-minute practice at Veikkaus Arena [165].

news.h: Brind'Amour wants the Helsinki games played for Carolina's Finns and for Ehlers
news.body: Nikolaj Ehlers, whose family and friends travel from Denmark for the games, has 15 points (four goals, 11 assists) in 19 games for a Carolina side that leads the NHL on 30 points at 14-3-2 [167]. In NHL.com's story of Tue 10 Nov, Brind’Amour said: “there’s this underlying story that’s going on here that we need to play for these guys because it’s not once in a lifetime, but almost” [167]. Carolina is the designated road team at Veikkaus Arena on Thursday at 18:00 CET and the home team on Saturday at 19:00 CET [1].

news.h: New Jersey loses at Winnipeg, and Carolina stays four points clear in the Metro
news.body: The Devils lost 4–2 at Winnipeg on Tue 10 Nov and stay on 26 points from 19 games, four behind Carolina's 30 from 19 [163, 168]. Washington won 3–2 in overtime at Ottawa and is fourth in the division on 20 points from 16 games [163, 168]. Seattle, Carolina's opponent in Helsinki, is fourth in the Pacific Division at 9-6-1 [168].

saints.h: Saints lose center Erik McCoy to a biceps injury before the Panthers visit
saints.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said on Mon 9 Nov that starting center Erik McCoy, hurt late in the 23–22 overtime win over Cleveland, will miss time: “We anticipate Erik being out for a little bit, and we'll just manage that on a week-to-week basis” [169]. Moore called it “not a long-term thing” and did not think McCoy needed surgery [169]. Carolina visit the Caesars Superdome on Sun 15 Nov with both teams 3-5 and first place in the NFC South at stake [170].

saints.h: Saints trade defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to Jacksonville
saints.body: General manager Mickey Loomis traded Davon Godchaux to the Jaguars on Mon 9 Nov for future considerations [171]. Godchaux had 15 tackles in eight games this season [171]. ESPN's grades of the 18 deals made before Tuesday's 22:00 CET deadline list it as the Saints' only trade, though ESPN gives the return as a 2028 sixth-round pick [172].

cardinals.h: Wetherholt finishes third in NL Rookie of the Year voting
cardinals.body: Second baseman JJ Wetherholt finished third in the National League Rookie of the Year vote announced on MLB Network on Mon 9 Nov; the Reds' Sal Stewart won and the Mets' Carson Benge was second [173]. He drew 99 points and three of 30 first-place votes after 17 home runs and 14 steals in 15 attempts [173]. The labour deal expires at 23:59 ET on 1 Dec, and NBC Sports wrote on 30 Oct that it “seems all but certain that there will be a work stoppage and a lockout on December 2” [174].

football.body: The KNVB said Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey had withdrawn because both were “niet fit uit het afgelopen speelweekend gekomen” (“did not come through last weekend's matches fit”) [175]. On Tue 10 Nov head coach Xavi Hernández gave Brentford defender Sepp van den Berg his first call-up [176]. The Netherlands lead Nations League A group 2 on eight points from four games, level with Greece, with Germany on five [177]. Greece visit the Johan Cruijff ArenA on Fri 13 Nov and the group ends in Berlin on Mon 16 Nov, both at 20:45 CET [177]. football.body: Racing Genk dismissed the Danish coach Jess Thorup, in charge since July, and his assistant Imre Szabics on Tue 10 Nov [179]. otd.title: On this day · 11 November 1918
otd.body: At 5 a.m. on 11 November 1918 the armistice between Germany and the Allies was agreed in a railcar in the Forest of Compiègne. [184] Marshal Foch sent word that “Hostilities will be stopped on the entire front beginning at 11 o'clock, November 11th (French hour)”. [184] The US made Armistice Day a legal holiday in 1938 and renamed it Veterans Day on 1 June 1954, to honour veterans of all wars. [185] At Brunssum War Cemetery, where 328 British soldiers who fell in the liberation of Limburg in 1944–45 lie, the Poppy Day remembrance starts at 10:30 today. [186]

culture.title: Sint Maarten and the Elfde van de Elfde share one wet Wednesday
culture.body: Today is Sint Maarten, the name day of Martin of Tours, the Roman soldier who cut his cloak in two for a freezing beggar; children walk with lanterns early in the evening, a custom that long survived mainly in the northern provinces and Limburg. [4] Parkstad keeps the bonfires too: Schinveld ended its lantern walk with a Sint-Maartensvuur (Saint Martin's bonfire) on Tuesday. [5] Since the 11devande11de party began in Maastricht in 2000, Limburg also celebrates at 11:11: in Parkstad, Kerkrade opens the season with 11-11 Kirchroa, Brunssum at the Schobben café hall and Hoensbroek with its song contest at the castle. [187]
